repos.desc: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
repos.summary: 这是一个基于 Rust 的命令行工具，专为 AI 代理提供浏览器自动化能力。它通过 Chrome DevTools Protocol 控制浏览器，核心工作流是“快照-操作-验证”：先用 `snapshot` 将页面转为可访问性树并生成元素引用（如 `@e1`），AI 随后通过 Shell 命令（如 `click @e1`）与页面交互，最后再次快照确认结果。
repos.judgment: 值得抄作业，它是目前将 LLM 与浏览器深度结合的 Rust 方案中体验较好的选择
mechanics: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) 控制浏览器
Accessibility Tree 快照机制（将 DOM 转为文本引用）
元素引用系统（Ref，如 @e1）用于精确定位
后台守护进程架构（保持浏览器会话存活）
MCP (Model Context Protocol) 服务器支持
Skills 技能系统（预定义的 AI 工作流）
scenarios: 开发需要自主浏览网页的 AI 代理（如自动化数据采集、预订系统）
构建基于 LLM 的 Web 应用自动化测试工具
集成 MCP 协议的 AI 助手需要直接操作浏览器 DOM 时

repos.desc: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
repos.summary: 这是一个让编码代理自动执行多阶段安全审计的技能，通过6个阶段（侦察、狩猎、验证、结构化输出、独立验证、报告）生成机器可读的漏洞发现结果。它使用零依赖的 Node.js 验证器确保数据完整性，并支持 Cloudflare 风格的对抗性验证和覆盖率驱动狩猎，最终输出 JSON 格式的审计报告。
repos.judgment: 值得抄作业，但需要强大的代理能力和严格的沙盒环境支持。
mechanics: 多阶段编排工作流：通过6个阶段（侦察、狩猎、验证、结构化输出、独立验证、报告）将审计流程标准化。
对抗性验证机制：验证漏洞的代理与发现漏洞的代理完全独立，防止自我确认偏差。
覆盖率驱动狩猎：基于 `coverage-ledger.json` 分配狩猎任务，确保不遗漏攻击面。
结构化输出与 Schema 验证：输出结果严格遵循 `report-schema.json`，通过 `validate-findings.cjs` 进行零依赖校验。
独立记录验证：对最终源代码声明进行二次独立验证，材料替换需触发额外验证。
模块化提示工程：按攻击类别（Web、AI、供应链等）组织提示词，支持并行子代理。
scenarios: 安全研究员/渗透测试人员：利用 AI 代理进行自动化代码审计，提高漏洞发现效率。
DevOps/开发团队：在 CI/CD 流程中集成安全检查，获取机器可读的 JSON 格式发现结果。
Cloudflare 风格的大规模漏洞挖掘：复现 Cloudflare 的漏洞发现工具链，进行多轮迭代审计。
需要严格审计合规的场景：利用对抗性验证和独立记录验证机制，确保审计结果的客观性。

repos.readmeCN:
# Skills For Real Engineers

[](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills)

My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding.

Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve.

These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter:

[Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter)

## Installation (30-second setup)

A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice.

### 1. Get the skills

Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official
```

Updates itself by default.

Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills
codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock
```

Updates itself at startup.

GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code)

```bash
copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills
copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock
```

Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true }
  }
}
```

In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.

Gemini CLI (manual updates)

```bash
gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering
gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity
```

Re-run both commands to update.

Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates)

```bash
npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a   # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose
```

When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.

### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`

In your agent, run it once per repo. It will:

- Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe)
- Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels)
- Ask you where you want to save any docs we create

### 3. Bam - you're ready to go.

## Why These Skills Exist

I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents.

### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want

> "No-one knows exactly what they want"
>
> David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V)

**The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all.

This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building.

**The Fix** is to use:

- [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses
- [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below)

These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change.

### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose

> With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model.
>
> Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215)

**The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages.

repos.readmeCN:
# Astryx

An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now:  by people and the agents working alongside them.

**Currently in Beta** · Built on [React 19+](https://react.dev) and [StyleX](https://stylexjs.com)

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@astryxdesign/core)
[](LICENSE)
[](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)

[](https://astryx.atmeta.com)
[](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)
[](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)

**[Docs](https://astryx.atmeta.com)** · **[Storybook](https://astryx.atmeta.com/storybook/)** · **[Sandbox](https://astryx.atmeta.com/sandbox/)** · **[Contributing](https://github.com/meta/astryx/wiki/Contributing)** · **[Discord](https://discord.com/invite/XnsUcFykEP)**

## Overview

Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling.

**What makes Astryx different:**

- **Open internals.** Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own.
- **No styling lock-in.** Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with `className` using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses.
- **Customize without wrapping.** A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source.
- **Built for people and agents.** The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference.

## Getting Started

Astryx requires **React 19** or later (`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies of `@astryxdesign/core`).

Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies:

```bash
# npm
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli

# pnpm
pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli

# yarn
yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli
```

You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so `astryx` works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version:

```bash
npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli
```

Project install, global install, or both? `astryx docs global/project-global-or-both` compares them (both is recommended), and `astryx docs global` explains how global mode works.

The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the **[@astryxdesign/core README](packages/core/README.md#quick-start)** for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN).

For reliable CLI access, add a script to your `package.json`:

```json
"scripts": {
  "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs"
}
```

Then use it as `npm run astryx -- component --list`. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly.

## Packages

| Package                                    | Description                                                                                          | README                             |

| [`@astryxdesign/core`](packages/core)      | Components, theme system, and utilities                                                              | [README](packages/core/README.md)  |

repos.readmeCN:
Prometheus

Visit prometheus.io for the full documentation,
examples and guides.

[](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[][quay]
[][hub]
[](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/486)
[](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yml)
[](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/prometheus/prometheus)
[](https://clomonitor.io/projects/cncf/prometheus)
[](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/list?sort=-opened&can=1&q=proj:prometheus)

Prometheus, a [Cloud Native Computing Foundation](https://cncf.io/) project, is a systems and service monitoring system. It collects metrics
from configured targets at given intervals, evaluates rule expressions,
displays the results, and can trigger alerts when specified conditions are observed.

The features that distinguish Prometheus from other metrics and monitoring systems are:

* A **multi-dimensional** data model (time series defined by metric name and set of key/value dimensions)
* PromQL, a **powerful and flexible query language** to leverage this dimensionality
* No dependency on distributed storage; **single server nodes are autonomous**
* An HTTP **pull model** for time series collection
* **Pushing time series** is supported via an intermediary gateway for batch jobs
* Targets are discovered via **service discovery** or **static configuration**
* Multiple modes of **graphing and dashboarding support**

* Support for hierarchical and horizontal **federation**

## Architecture overview

## Install

There are various ways to install Prometheus.

### Precompiled binaries

Precompiled binaries for released versions are available in the
[*download* section](https://prometheus.io/download/)
on [prometheus.io](https://prometheus.io). Using the latest production release binary
is the recommended way to install Prometheus.
See the [Installing](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/install/)
chapter in the documentation for all the details.

### Docker images

Docker images are available on [Quay.io](https://quay.io/repository/prometheus/prometheus) or [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/prom/prometheus/).

You can launch a Prometheus container for trying it out with

```bash
docker run --name prometheus -d -p 127.0.0.1:9090:9090 prom/prometheus
```

Prometheus will now be reachable at .

### Building from source

To build Prometheus from source code, you need:

* Go: Version specified in [go.mod](./go.mod) or greater.
* NodeJS: Version specified in [.nvmrc](./web/ui/.nvmrc) or greater.
* npm: Version 10 or greater (check with `npm --version` and [here](https://www.npmjs.com/)).

Start by cloning the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus.git
cd prometheus
```

You can use the `go` tool to build and install the `prometheus`
and `promtool` binaries into your `GOPATH`:

```bash
go install github.com/prometheus/prometheus/cmd/...
prometheus --config.file=your_config.yml
```

*However*, when using `go install` to build Prometheus, Prometheus will expect to be able to
read its web assets from local filesystem directories under `web/ui/static`. In order for
these assets to be found, you will have to run Prometheus from the root of the cloned
repository. Note also that this directory does not include the React UI unless it has been
built explicitly using `make assets` or `make build`.

An example of the above configuration file can be found [here.](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/documentation/examples/prometheus.yml)

You can also build using `make build`, which will compile in the web assets so that
Prometheus can be run from anywhere:

```bash
make build
./prometheus --config.file=your_config.yml
```

The Makefile provides several targets:

* *build*: build the `prometheus` and `promtool` binaries (includes building and compiling in web assets)
* *test*: run the tests
* *test-short*: run the short tests
* *format*: format the source code
* *vet*: check the source code for common errors
* *assets*: build the React UI

### Service discovery plugins

Prometheus is bundled with many service discovery plugins. You can customize
which service discoveries are included in your build using Go build tags.

To exclude service discoveries when building with `make build`, add the desired
tags to the `.promu.yml` file under `build.tags.all`:

```yaml
build:
    tags:
        all:
            - netgo
            - builtinassets
            - remove_all_sd           # Exclude all optional SDs
            - enable_kubernetes_sd    # Re-enable only kubernetes
```

repos.desc: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
repos.summary: Sherlock 是一个开源的 OSINT 工具，通过向 400 多个社交网络发送 HTTP 请求来验证用户名是否存在。它支持批量搜索、代理设置以及导出 TXT、CSV、XLSX 等多种格式的结果文件。
repos.judgment: 值得抄作业，但需注意第三方包维护状态及合规性，建议使用 Docker 或 pipx 安装。
mechanics: HTTP 请求扫描：通过向目标社交网站的特定 URL 发送请求并比对响应内容来判断用户名是否存在。
本地数据驱动：依赖 `data.json` 文件存储站点列表和检测逻辑，支持 `--local` 强制使用本地数据。
代理支持：支持通过 SOCKS5 或 HTTP 代理进行请求，以绕过 IP 限制或隐藏身份。

scenarios: 开源情报调查：安全研究员或调查人员寻找目标在多个平台的公开账号。

个人验证：用户检查自己常用的用户名是否已被他人占用。
安全审计：检查账号是否在多个平台泄露，评估风险。

mechanics: Bring your own agents (BYO Agents)：利用用户本地已安装的 CLI（如 claude、codex）作为后端引擎，无需额外注册账号或通过代理中转。

repos.desc: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.
repos.summary: Ruff 是一个用 Rust 编写的极快 Python 代码检查器和格式化工具，能直接替代 Flake8、Black、isort 等多个工具。安装后通过 `ruff check` 进行静态检查，通过 `ruff format` 进行代码格式化，支持自动修复和缓存。
repos.judgment: 值得抄作业，它是目前 Python 生态中最快的代码质量工具，强烈推荐升级。
mechanics: Rust 编写：利用 Rust 的高性能特性，比传统 Python 工具快 10-100 倍。
AST 解析：基于抽象语法树进行静态分析，而非正则匹配。
规则重实现：原生实现了 Flake8、isort、Black 等工具的规则集。
缓存机制：内置缓存，避免重复分析未修改的文件。
自动修复：支持 `--fix` 参数自动修正代码问题。
scenarios: Python 项目代码质量检查：在本地开发或 CI 流水线中替代 Flake8。
代码格式化：统一团队代码风格，替代 Black 和 isort。
编辑器集成：在 VS Code 等编辑器中实时检查和格式化代码。
大型代码库维护：处理大型项目时，利用极速性能减少等待时间。

repos.readmeCN:
# LocalThings

**Control your Samsung appliances from Home Assistant over your home network, with no cloud account.**

LocalThings connects Home Assistant to Samsung washers, dryers, refrigerators, air conditioners, ovens and other appliances that work with the SmartThings app. It talks to each appliance on your local network.

- **Updates are fast.** Appliances that support push send changes as they happen. LocalThings checks the rest every 30 seconds.
- **It works without the internet.** After setup, LocalThings never contacts Samsung's servers.
- **Your data stays home.** LocalThings sends nothing to Samsung. The appliance itself still keeps its own connection to Samsung, and LocalThings doesn't change that.
- **Setup needs an IP address.** For most appliances, you enter the address and LocalThings works out the type and model, then creates matching controls and sensors.

## What it supports

| Appliance | Appliance |

| Air conditioner, including multi-unit systems | Microwave |
| Air dresser | Oven |
| Air monitor | Range and range hood |
| Air purifier | Refrigerator, kimchi refrigerator, wine cellar |
| Cooktop, gas, radiant electric and induction; some models read-only | Robot vacuum, early support |
| Dehumidifier | Soundbar, settings and status |
| Dishwasher | Vacuum clean station |
| Dryer | Washer and washer-dryer |
| EHS heat pump | Water purifier |

What you see depends on what each appliance reports. Typical controls and sensors include power, program or mode selection, start, pause and stop, temperatures and setpoints, time remaining and finish time, door and child-lock state, energy use, filter status and alarms.

Most Samsung appliances from about 2022 onward work, and so do some earlier washers, air conditioners and wall ovens that use an older local interface. See [Older appliances on TCP 8888](#older-appliances-on-tcp-8888). Setup detects which interface an appliance has, and tells you if it finds none.

If an appliance sets up but LocalThings doesn't recognize it, or a control is missing, Home Assistant shows a notice asking for a diagnostics download. That download is usually all the maintainers need to add support. See [Reporting a capability gap](#reporting-a-capability-gap).

## Built on open standards

LocalThings uses the standards the appliances implement:

- **OCF, the [Open Connectivity Foundation](https://openconnectivity.org/) specification.** Samsung's connected appliances are OCF devices. LocalThings discovers each appliance's resources through `/oic/res` and reads its device type, such as `oic.d.washer`, from `/oic/d`. Where an appliance offers both a standard OCF resource and a Samsung extension for the same state, LocalThings uses the standard one.

- **CoAP over DTLS.** LocalThings sends Constrained Application Protocol requests, defined in [RFC 7252](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7252), over an encrypted DTLS session with an X.509 client certificate. It uses CoAP Observe, [RFC 7641](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7641), for push updates, and block-wise transfer, [RFC 7959](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7959), for large responses. The [`smartthings-local`](https://github.com/QuiteYellow/SmartThings-Local) library implements the protocol layer.
- **Home Assistant's own patterns.** Setup, reconfigure and reauthentication run in the UI config flow. A data-update coordinator combines push and polling. DHCP discovery follows an appliance to a new IP address. Repairs notices report gaps. LocalThings redacts diagnostics downloads and translates entity names into ten languages.
- **Declarative appliance maps.** Each appliance type is a table that maps the resources an appliance reports to Home Assistant entities. Tests check the tables against 90+ captures from real appliances, so a new model usually needs a table entry and no protocol code.

---

## Install

1. In [HACS](https://hacs.xyz/), go to **Integrations**, search for **LocalThings**, and select **Download**. LocalThings is in HACS's default list, so you don't need to add a custom repository.

   [](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=mbillow&repository=localthings&category=integration)

# Zed

[](https://zed.dev)
[](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/actions/workflows/run_tests.yml)

Welcome to Zed, a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of [Atom](https://github.com/atom/atom) and [Tree-sitter](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter).

---

### Installation

On macOS, Linux, and Windows you can [download Zed directly](https://zed.dev/download) or install Zed via your local package manager ([macOS](https://zed.dev/docs/installation#macos)/[Linux](https://zed.dev/docs/linux#installing-via-a-package-manager)/[Windows](https://zed.dev/docs/windows#package-managers)).

Other platforms are not yet available:

- Web ([tracking discussion](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/discussions/26195))

### Developing Zed

- [Building Zed for macOS](./docs/src/development/macos.md)
- [Building Zed for Linux](./docs/src/development/linux.md)
- [Building Zed for Windows](./docs/src/development/windows.md)

### Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for ways you can contribute to Zed.

Also... we're hiring! Check out our [jobs](https://zed.dev/jobs) page for open roles.

### Licensing

Zed source code is licensed primarily under GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components where marked.

License information for third party dependencies must be correctly provided for CI to pass.

We use [`cargo-about`](https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-about) to automatically comply with open source licenses. If CI is failing, check the following:

- Is it showing a `no license specified` error for a crate you've created? If so, add `publish = false` under `[package]` in your crate's Cargo.toml.
- Is the error `failed to satisfy license requirements` for a dependency? If so, first determine what license the project has and whether this system is sufficient to comply with this license's requirements. If you're unsure, ask a lawyer. Once you've verified that this system is acceptable add the license's SPDX identifier to the `accepted` array in `script/licenses/zed-licenses.toml`.
- Is `cargo-about` unable to find the license for a dependency? If so, add a clarification field at the end of `script/licenses/zed-licenses.toml`, as specified in the [cargo-about book](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-about/cli/generate/config.html#crate-configuration).

## Sponsorship

Zed is developed by **Zed Industries, Inc.**, a for-profit company.

If you’d like to financially support the project, you can do so via GitHub Sponsors.
Sponsorships go directly to Zed Industries and are used as general company revenue.
There are no perks or entitlements associated with sponsorship.

repos.desc: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE). A management plane for GPU Kubernetes on bare metal.
repos.summary: NVIDIA Kubernetes引擎(NVKE)。裸机上GPU Kubernetes的管理平面。
repos.judgment: NVIDIA Kubernetes引擎(NVKE)。裸机上GPU Kubernetes的管理平面。
repos.readmeCN:
# NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE)

[](LICENSE)
[](go.work)

**Run a managed Kubernetes service on your own NVIDIA GPU infrastructure.**
NVIDIA Kubernetes® Engine (NVKE) provides the management plane that platform teams install to create and
operate Kubernetes clusters for their customers. Each workload cluster has its
own Kubernetes control plane, etcd and node pools. You operate the NVKE management
plane; your customers use their clusters through the Kubernetes API and `kubectl`.

> **Preview:** NVKE is available as a preview. APIs, configuration and behavior
> can change between releases, and we do not recommend NVKE for production
> workloads. See [Preview status and known limitations](docs/overview/preview-status.md).

[Get started](#getting-started) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) ·
[Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Get help](SUPPORT.md)

## Getting started

| Your goal | Start here | What you get |

| **Evaluate without GPU hardware** | [Local quickstart](docs/get-started/quickstart-local.md) | A development management plane and a workload cluster on simulated machines. No NVIDIA account is required. |
| **Install on your infrastructure** | [Plan your installation](docs/operate/plan-installation.md) | The prerequisites and sequence for preparing nodes, bootstrapping a management cluster and installing its services. |
| **Build or contribute** | [Build from source](#build-from-source) | The NVKE binaries and the contributor development loop. |

The local quickstart runs on a **Linux host or VM, amd64 or arm64**, with at least
**6 CPUs, 12 GiB of free memory and 100 GiB of free disk**. It requires Docker,
virtual TPM support and the tools listed in the guide. Follow its setup through
workload-cluster creation and confirm the cluster's nodes report `Ready`.
On macOS, use the [local site guide](docs/get-started/local-site.md), which runs
the evaluation inside a Colima virtual machine.

For a real installation, you supply the machines, networking, node images and
registries, and configure access to **NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo)**. NICo is
the sole compatible infrastructure provider at preview. The
[platform and version reference](docs/overview/supported-platforms.md) lists
validated combinations and pinned dependencies.

## What NVKE does

- **Creates independent workload clusters.** Request clusters through the NVKE
  API or `nvkectl`; NVKE provisions machines through NICo and forms Kubernetes
  clusters with their own control planes.
- **Manages workload cluster lifecycle.** Create, scale and delete node pools,
  upgrade Kubernetes and replace nodes. See the [node pool guide](docs/workload-clusters/node-pools.md)
  for the manual steps and preview limits on replacement and upgrades.
- **Establishes node identity.** Nodes attest through SPIFFE/SPIRE using their
  TPM before receiving join credentials. Encryption of etcd data is available
  per cluster.
- **Connects builds to deployment.** Its companion project,

[NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR)](https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/nvkr),
  builds node images and NVKE components from pinned inputs. NVKE deploys those
  artifacts; NVKR owns their build and release evidence.

The preview needs explicit operator configuration: API authentication is off
and the API uses plain HTTP after installation. Configure
[API authentication and protected access](docs/operate/api-authentication.md)
before admitting callers. The management cluster does not upgrade, scale or
replace itself, and there is no management-plane upgrade or backup/restore
procedure. FDE node images are for evaluation and provide no data-at-rest
confidentiality. Read the [known limitations](docs/overview/preview-status.md)
before choosing an evaluation or installation path.

## Overview

The diagram shows the NVKE product family, how it sits on NICo and your GPU machines, and which components talk to each other.

NVKE is not a Kubernetes distribution and not a Cluster API flavour. It is a
**self-hosting factory for Kubernetes clusters**: a throwaway seed cluster
stands up a management cluster, and the management plane on
it then provisions and lifecycle-manages many isolated workload clusters
on demand.

An installation has two kinds of Kubernetes cluster:

- The **management cluster** runs the NVKE management plane and infrastructure
  controllers. `nvkectl` forms it using a temporary seed cluster; installing the
  management-plane services is a separate step.

featured.desc: A research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference. Not maintained.
featured.summary: 这是一个研究原型，允许 AI 提供商在不暴露模型权重的情况下，证明其推理结果确实来自承诺的模型。它通过发布承诺 ID、GPU 生成证明、CPU 验证证明的流程，让用户确认服务端使用的模型身份。
featured.judgment: 不值得抄作业，这是未维护的研究原型，硬件门槛极高且构建复杂。
mechanics: 零知识证明 (ZKP) 架构：通过数学证明而非直接比对权重来验证模型身份
承诺机制：将模型权重绑定到一个承诺 ID，ID 公开但权重保密
Lean 4 形式化验证：在 Lean 中证明了协议的可靠性，错误概率极低
GPU 加速证明生成：利用 NVIDIA H100 80GB 显卡在几秒内生成证明
独立验证器：`cp_verify` 程序可在普通 CPU 上运行，无需加载模型权重
支持 Llama 4 Maverick：全尺寸模型，1,024 token 上下文窗口
scenarios: AI 服务提供商需要向客户证明其承诺的模型（如 Llama 4 Maverick）确实在运行，防止模型切换欺诈
企业或监管机构验证 AI 服务提供商的合规性与安全性
研究人员验证零知识证明在大型语言模型推理中的可行性与性能
验证特定 AI 模型输出的真实性，而不需要获取模型的内部参数

featured.summary: 这是一个 Python 工具包，旨在将复杂的“路由器+多个子代理”多智能体架构，通过评估指标逐步重构为“单智能体循环”架构。它包含一个 Claude Code 技能，能自动审计代码、构建评估基准并执行折叠操作。
featured.judgment: 适合用于实验性的多智能体架构重构研究，但因其非维护状态，不建议直接用于关键生产环境。
mechanics: 评估驱动迁移：不盲目合并，而是通过对比基准测试分数来决定是否移除子代理。
Claude Code Skill 自动化：skill/ 目录是一个可执行的技能，能自动分析代码、生成评估任务并执行折叠计划。
单智能体循环架构：参考实现展示了如何用并行工具批处理、按需加载技能和预算控制来替代子代理。
耦合度分析：使用 coupling_map.py 分析追踪数据，识别总是同时运行的子代理以便合并。
链路覆盖率检查：确保评估任务覆盖了所有生产流程中的子代理调用链路。
scenarios: 拥有多智能体系统且希望简化架构、降低上下文窗口成本的团队。
已经有评估框架，需要量化架构变更（如折叠子代理）对性能和成本影响的开发者。
使用 Claude Code 作为主要交互工具的项目。
正在研究“单智能体循环”架构可行性的实验性项目。

featured.summary: 这是一个由 Anthropic 提供的自动化开源安全扫描服务。用户通过向仓库提交 PR 添加 `projects/<name>` 目录（包含配置文件和 Dockerfile），服务会在隔离的虚拟机中构建项目并扫描漏洞，最终将包含复现步骤和补丁建议的报告发送给项目联系人。
featured.judgment: 这是一个针对开源项目的“黑盒”安全审计服务，适合不想自建扫描器但愿意通过 PR 提交配置的项目维护者，但无法本地运行且依赖 Dockerfile。
mechanics: 隔离构建与扫描：先在有网环境构建项目，再移至无网环境进行扫描，确保扫描环境纯净。
Dockerfile 驱动：扫描器完全依赖用户提供的 Dockerfile 来构建环境和安装依赖。
威胁模型引导：通过 `threat_model.md` 文件定义安全目标和严重性评级标准。
私有漏洞报告：集成 GitHub 私有漏洞报告 API，通过 `oss-scanner` 账号发送报告。
本地验证工具：提供 `tools/check` 和 `tools/validate.py`，允许用户在提交前在本地模拟构建和测试。
scenarios: 开源项目维护者希望获得专业的自动化安全审计，但不想自建扫描基础设施。
需要定期进行安全扫描但缺乏内部安全团队的项目。
需要针对特定项目定制扫描策略（通过威胁模型）的团队。

featured.summary: 这是一个 Anthropic DevRel 团队维护的 Claude Code 演示与配置集合，包含真实的 `CLAUDE.md`、`settings.json`、Hooks、Mods 和工作流示例。每个条目都是独立的，用户只需打开对应文件夹并遵循其 README 中的“Run it”指令即可直接运行。
featured.judgment: 值得作为学习参考，但需注意非官方维护和可能失效的风险。

开发自定义 Hooks 或 Mods 寻找参考实现
准备发布会 Demo 或 Art-of-the-possible 演示

featured.summary: 这是一个包含36个针对蛋白质和基因组AI模型（如结构预测、语言模型）的“开箱即用”推理优化工具包集合。每个工具对应一个独立目录，通过运行脚本或环境变量一键切换优化模式（如fast、exact、big），无需修改原始代码即可加速推理或降低显存占用。
featured.judgment: 适合想快速体验或实验性使用这些优化，但不要指望长期维护和闭源生产。
mechanics: 模式切换机制：定义了off（原版）、exact（同输出加速）、fast（可接受差异加速）、big（低显存/多GPU）四种统一模式。
模块化架构：每个kit目录包含stock（上游原版）、opt（优化包）和共享核心，互不干扰。
共享内核：`common/opt_core` 提供通用的模式解析、确定性辅助、多GPU调度和自定义GPU内核（如FlashPairformer）。
容器化部署：支持Docker和Apptainer两种容器方案，确保环境一致性。
库风格集成：对于库类工具，通过环境变量（如`<KIT>_OPT=exact`）或API调用启用优化，无需修改调用脚本。
scenarios: 生物信息学研究人员需要快速运行蛋白质结构预测（如AlphaFold变体）并希望获得比官方更快的推理速度。
在显存受限的GPU服务器上运行大型基因组语言模型（如ESM），需要使用 `big` 模式降低峰值显存或分片到多卡。
开发者希望在现有代码库中集成优化，而不想重写底层推理逻辑，只需设置环境变量即可。
需要在不同计算环境（Docker或Apptainer）中复现相同的优化效果。
